the other of Rav Yehuda / Rav Eina (50b.1, וחד תני חשובה)
the Sages disputing R' Yosei bar Yehuda in the 50b.2 and 51a.8 baraitot
R' Yehuda HaNasi, disqualifying wooden service vessels (50b.3)
the flute mishna, Sukkah 50a.6, read by the stam at 51a.11

props.gloss_en: one teaches [the celebration's name as] sho'eva
and one teaches chashuva
Mar Zutra: the one who teaches sho'eva is not mistaken, as it is written 'and you shall draw water with joy' (Isa 12:3)
Rav Nachman: it is a significant mitzva, and it comes from the six days of creation
Mar Zutra: the one who teaches chashuva is not mistaken, as Rav Nachman said it is a significant mitzva
the flute overrides Shabbat -- R' Yosei bar Yehuda
and the Sages say: it does not override even Yom Tov
Rav Yosef: the dispute is about the song of the offering
the essence of [the Temple] song is the instrument
the essence of [the Temple] song is the mouth
the song of the offering is service and overrides Shabbat
the song of the offering is not service and does not override Shabbat
R' Yosei [bar Yehuda]'s reason: the song is essentially instrumental, so [the playing] is service, so it overrides
the Rabbis' reason: the song is essentially vocal, so [the playing] is not service and does not override
Rav Yosef: but the song of the Drawing -- all agree it is rejoicing and does not override Shabbat
service vessels made of wood: Rebbi disqualifies
and R' Yosei bar Yehuda validates
Rav Yosef: is it not about this [the essence of the song] that they disagree?
and we derive [wooden service vessels' validity] from Moses's flute
and we do not derive [anything] from Moses's flute
[all agree the song is instrumental;] here they disagree whether one derives the possible from the impossible
the validator holds one derives the possible from the impossible
the disqualifier holds one does not derive the possible from the impossible

[all agree the song is vocal and one does not derive the possible from the impossible;] here they disagree whether the menorah is expounded by generalizations-and-details or by amplifications-and-restrictions
Rebbi expounds generalizations and details
R' Yosei bar Yehuda expounds amplifications and restrictions
Rebbi: generalization, detail, generalization -- judge only by the likeness of the detail: as the detail is metal, so all [the vessel] of metal
R' Yosei bar Yehuda: amplification, restriction, amplification -- it amplified everything: every material
and what did it restrict? [a menorah] of earthenware
Rav Pappa: [the dispute over the essence of the song] is like [a dispute of] tannaim
R' Meir: [the musicians] were slaves of priests
R' Yosei: from the families of Beit HaPegarim and Beit Tzipperaya, from Emmaus, who married into the priesthood
R' Chanina ben Antigonus: they were Levites
rather: all agree the essence of the song is the mouth; they disagree over what actually happened
what difference does it make? they disagree whether one raises [a family] from the platform to lineage and to tithes
the one who said slaves holds: one does not raise from the platform to lineage nor to tithes
the one who said Israelites holds: one raises from the platform to lineage, but not to tithes
the one who said Levites holds: one raises from the platform both to lineage and to tithes
the dispute is about the song of the Drawing of the Water
R' Yosei bar Yehuda holds: extra rejoicing also overrides Shabbat
the Rabbis hold: extra rejoicing does not override Shabbat
the song of the Drawing overrides Shabbat -- R' Yosei bar Yehuda
and the Sages say: it does not override even Yom Tov
Rav Yosef: they are shown disputing the Drawing's song to tell you R' Yosei bar Yehuda's force -- even the Drawing's overrides
the mishna: this is the flute of the Beit HaShoeva, which does not override Shabbat
the stam's inference: THIS one does not override -- but the [flute] of the offering does
whose is the mishna? not R' Yosei bar Yehuda, who says the Drawing's song also overrides; so the Rabbis
the instrumental view's reason: 'and when the burnt-offering began, the song of the Lord began, and the trumpets, by the instruments of David' (II Chr 29:27)
the vocal view's reason: 'and the trumpeters and the singers were as one, to make one sound heard' (II Chr 5:13)
this is what it says: the song of the Lord began -- by mouth; by the instruments of David -- to sweeten the sound
this is what it says: the singers are like the trumpeters -- as the trumpeters [play] by instrument, so the singers by instrument

deflected_by.gloss_en: לא, דכולי עלמא עיקר שירה בכלי, והכא בדנין אפשר משאי אפשר קמיפלגי (= p_kli_etz_hinges_danin)

challenges.gloss_en: מיתיבי: שיר של שואבה דוחה את השבת, דברי רבי יוסי בר יהודה, וחכמים אומרים אף יום טוב אינו דוחה -- תיובתא דרב יוסף! תיובתא

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך רב יוסף: פליגי בשיר של שואבה, והוא הדין לקרבן; והאי דקמיפלגי בשיר של שואבה -- להודיעך כחו דרבי יוסי בר יהודה (= p_lehodiacha_kocho)
